set_title: Pericarditis vs endocarditis names: which layer and what is growing on the valve
stem: A 28-year-old woman with a malar rash, arthralgia and positive anti-dsDNA antibodies has a new murmur. Three sets of blood cultures are negative. Echocardiography shows small warty growths on both the atrial and ventricular surfaces of the mitral valve.
oneliner: 28-year-old woman, SLE, negative cultures, growths on both sides of mitral valve → ?

whyNot.A: Usually fever with positive cultures; hers are **negative** with **SLE features**
whyNot.C: Occurs with cancer and clots on the closure line; she has **SLE features**
whyNot.D: Follows strep with Jones criteria; she has **malar rash and anti-dsDNA antibodies**
whyNot.E: Causes positional pain and ST elevation; she has **warty mitral valve growths**

why: Named for Libman and Sacks, who described sterile warty valve growths in lupus. **SLE with negative cultures and growths on both mitral surfaces** is typical.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Pain better leaning forward; diffuse ST elevation**
**Advanced cancer; sterile clots on closure line**
post-strep inflammation of all heart layers

idea.rule: Libman-Sacks = lupus, sterile, both valve surfaces. Marantic = cancer, sterile, closure line.
also: Verrucous growths on both valve surfaces

set_title: -ectasia words: something widened (telangiectasia, duct ectasia, lymphangiectasia)
stem: A 3-year-old boy has had an unsteady walk for a year and repeated sinus and lung infections. He has dilated red vessels on the whites of both eyes. Serum IgA is low.
oneliner: 3-year-old boy, unsteady gait + sinopulmonary infections + red conjunctival vessels + low IgA → ?

whyNot.B: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia brings nosebleeds and AVMs; he has **unsteady gait and low IgA**
whyNot.C: Mammary duct ectasia affects adult breasts; he is a **3-year-old boy**
whyNot.D: Intestinal lymphangiectasia causes edema and diarrhea, not **ataxia with low IgA**
whyNot.E: Bronchiectasis is airway widening; it does not explain the **unsteady gait and eye vessels**

why: Ataxia (incoordination) + telangiectasia (widened tiny vessels): an ATM DNA-repair defect. **Ataxia, eye telangiectasia and low IgA with sinopulmonary infections** fit.

idea.rule: Ataxia-telangiectasia: the name lists the two main signs.

set_title: Broncho- names: bronchiolitis, bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchopulmonary dysplasia and their look-alikes
stem: A 52-year-old man had a bilateral lung transplant 2 years ago for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Over 4 months he has had worsening shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough, with no fever. His FEV1 has fallen 30% from its best value after the transplant, the FEV1/FVC ratio is low, and a bronchodilator does not change it. Expiratory CT images show patchy air trapping, and the airways are not dilated.
oneliner: 52M, lung transplant 2 years ago + slow dyspnea, falling FEV1 not reversed by bronchodilator + air trapping → ?

whyNot.A: Bronchiolitis strikes infants acutely; he is **52 with 4 months of slow decline**
whyNot.B: Bronchiectasis dilates airways with copious sputum; his **airways are not dilated**, cough dry
whyNot.D: Bronchogenic cyst is a single mediastinal mass; he has **patchy air trapping throughout**
whyNot.E: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia affects ventilated preterm newborns; he is **52, 2 years post-transplant**

why: Small airway inflammation + closing off: the bronchioles scar shut. **Fixed FEV1 fall with air trapping after lung transplant** is chronic rejection.

head: Means
One clue
rows: **Infant's winter cold moving down to wheeze**
**Preterm, ventilated, still on oxygen at 36 weeks**
**Daily purulent sputum; airway wider than artery**

idea.rule: New fixed obstruction after lung or stem cell transplant = bronchiolitis obliterans.
also: Leading cause of late death after lung transplant
Also after GVHD, adenovirus, Mycoplasma or fumes
